main_text.p: lepticis ad prolem transfertur, infanabilis quoq; merito habenda est. In hac enim maxime omnium illucet summa cerebri imbecillitas. Vertiginosę[?] quoq;, ut & quibus magna spiradi difficultas adest, aut totius corporis magna refrigeratio, cum comate, & mouendi debilitate, uix, aut egerrimè depelluntur. Eas silentio non praetereo, quæ errhinis, odoratisúe naribus admotis non cedunt. Cæteris autem omnibus spes salutis adest, si singulis sua & propria adhibean-tur remedia. Primarias epilepsias deprehendunt bitumē suffitu, aut gagates lapis, aut caprini cornu fumus, aut hircini hepatis asfi nidor, aut idem commanducatum.
main_text.head: EXERC. XXXVIII. MORBORVM COMITIALIVM curationes.
main_text.p: PRimùm ingruentem morbum depellemus sternutatorijs, & odoratis suffitibus admotis naribus, si primaria sit epilepsia, & per prothopathiam cerebri. Eiusmodi sunto radix albi hellebori, peucedanum & lafer naribus subditus. Iris quoq; naribus subducta sternutamenta mouet, non ea tamen, qua nùc utunt pharma-

page.notes: The first word of the page, "lepticis", is cut off at the left edge; the full word is probably "epilepticis", but only the visible fragment is transcribed. "Vertiginosę" is doubtful: the final letter is a small superscript form that I read as ę. The "s" forms in "sternutatorijs", "sunto" and "subditus" are read as long s, which I have written as plain s. The catchword "copolæ" is printed at the right below the last line, after the hyphenated "pharma-". The signature "M 2" is at the foot. The printed letters of the main text were checked against the scan, but the page is faint in places, so the readings "comate" and "lafer" should be verified.
